title: Pharmacist-led opioid tapering support in a multidisciplinary pain clinic: a prospective observational study
subtitle: Twelve-month follow-up of everyone entering the tapering pathway, Vellmoor General Hospital
statement: Adults on long-term opioids of 50 mg oral morphine equivalents a day or more who choose to taper at the Vellmoor pain clinic receive pharmacist-led support: a shared taper plan, fortnightly pharmacist calls, naloxone and rapid review. Whether the pathway is followed by meaningful dose reduction without worse pain interference, withdrawal distress, disengagement or overdose is not known locally. The study will describe 12-month outcomes for everyone entering the pathway over one year and identify who leaves it.
whoAffected: Adults tapering long-term opioids and their families, the clinic pharmacist and physicians, community pharmacists who dispense the tapered doses, and emergency department staff who see withdrawal or overdose.
whatHurts: Unsupported tapers can bring withdrawal, uncontrolled pain, loss of trust and, after fast reductions, overdose; staying on high doses carries its own risks. Patients who leave the pathway lose support at the point of highest risk, and the clinic does not know who they are.
currentPractice: Since July 2025 every eligible patient who wants to taper is offered the pathway; outcomes are written in the clinic notes but never summarised, and patients who stop answering calls are not followed up systematically.
whyNow: The hospital decides in 2027 whether to fund the pharmacist post beyond March 2028, and the first year of the pathway (88 patients) shows the clinic can enrol about seven patients a month.
constraints: 0.4 FTE pharmacist, no research funding, routine calls and visits only; every participant should reach a 25 percent dose reduction by 6 months so that the outcome is comparable across patients.
patientCenteredGoal: People who choose to taper reduce their opioid dose at a pace they agree to, with pain and daily life no worse, and nobody is lost from support without the clinic noticing.
summary: Problem framed as a prospective observational follow-up of the tapering pathway with dose, pain interference, withdrawal, disengagement and overdose outcomes.
